item.title: print_sprint_summary read prompt exits script via set -e when stdin is not a terminal
item.intent: The architecture review prompt in print_sprint_summary must not cause the script to exit when stdin is closed or non-interactive. The read call must be guarded so a non-tty or piped stdin produces a graceful skip, not a set -e triggered exit.
item.description: In print_sprint_summary (line ~3090), a bare 'read -r -p "..." _review_answer' runs when auto_review is not set. Bash 'read' returns exit code 1 when stdin is at EOF (CI, pipes, or non-interactive shells). Because the script uses 'set -euo pipefail', a failing read propagates as an unhandled error and exits the script mid-session. The fix is to append '|| true' to the read call, or to guard the entire block with '[[ -t 0 ]]' so the prompt is only shown in interactive sessions. The '|| true' approach is sufficient and minimal.
steps: Locate the 'read -r -p "  Run architecture review? [y/N] " _review_answer' call in print_sprint_summary (line ~3090)
Append '|| true' to make it: 'read -r -p "  Run architecture review? [y/N] " _review_answer || true'
Verify that in a non-interactive context (piped stdin), the function completes without error and skips the review
Verify that in an interactive context, the prompt still works correctly
Run shellcheck and confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Running 'echo "" | .aishore/aishore auto done' (piped stdin) does not exit with an error from the review prompt
In an interactive session with valid 'y' input, the architecture review is still triggered
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
